sampling_model.design: Two randomized regime studies report complete \(2\times2\) tables, one under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\) and one under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\).
sampling_model.units: The population version treats \(A\) and \(B\) as exact laws of one SCM; the optional sampling result uses multinomial frequency tables of sizes \(nA\) and \(nB\).
sampling_model.treatment: The first regime fixes \(Z=0\) and leaves \(X\) natural; the second fixes \(X=0\) and leaves \(Z\) natural.
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity or overlap condition is imposed on the population tables: normalization gives \(0\le a\le p\le1\) and \(0\le b\le r\le1\).  On any stratum with zero probability, feasibility forces its target-success numerator to zero and the construction assigns the unused conditional response arbitrarily.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated. The optional interval uses only empirical multinomial cells and simultaneous concentration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Minimization or maximization of the produced polynomial program gives sharp lower or upper bounds on the declared target.
Counterfactual consistency of overlapping categorical marginal SCMs restricts the admissible marginal and joint SCMs.
Every categorical SCM has a finite canonical SCM with the same graph and all the same counterfactual distributions.
EMCC returns fully specified compatible SCMs whose counterfactual range approximates the actual bounds from inside.
The global extrema of a response-function linear program occur at vertices of its feasible polytope.

body.tldr: For the fixed binary collider with two mutually independent shared roots and private outcome noise, arbitrary normalized experimental tables are compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\), and the all-zero joint-intervention risk has the proved sharp interval \([\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\},\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}]\).  One ordered-threshold private root with at most eight support points realizes every interval value while reproducing both complete tables, including all structural-zero faces.  The result yields constant-time endpoints, exact rational endpoint certificates, and a conservative optional sampling interval for this graph and intervention menu.

project_justification.gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query numerically, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be consistent, but neither checked line supplies the graph-specific compatibility frontier, analytic endpoints, or a small common-SCM witness.
project_justification.niche: The fixed binary collider collapses to four natural-treatment strata, yet source independence prevents the armwise completions and unrestricted latent couplings used in simpler partial-identification arguments.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber, proves a closed-simplex source-preserving threshold lift with explicit null-stratum branches, and packages the resulting iff test and max/min interval as an exact analytic certificate procedure.  For this fixed input and query the certificate can replace a call to Autobounds' generic polynomial optimizer, while Duarte et al.'s graph-general sharp-optimization theorem remains broader and is not claimed as a new contribution here.

body.related_work: Gresele et al. formulate structural causal marginal compatibility and explain why overlapping reports must share one response-function law.  Duarte et al., JASA 2024, prove that finite discrete causal bounds with observational or experimental constraints and product disturbance probabilities can be obtained sharply by generic polynomial optimization; their scope permits categorical laws on support faces.  The present result is a closed-simplex analytic specialization for one binary collider, two interventions, and one risk: it derives the compatibility inequality, closed-form endpoints, and small common-SCM certificates rather than strengthening the graph-general solver theorem.  Autobounds is therefore the same-input software consumer whose generic optimization can be replaced by this certificate on the stated specialization.  Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide graph-preserving finite canonical SCM representations, but not this eight-point menu-specific lift or formula.  Sachs et al. give symbolic response-function bounds under linear constraints, while the independent latent-source factorization here must be preserved explicitly.  Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, provide adjacent multi-source approximate inner bounding through causal EM rather than the exact compatibility and sharp closed-form result proved here.  Shridharan and Iyengar, Finkelstein and Shpitser, and Balke and Pearl provide related optimization, logical-bound, and response-type machinery, but no checked result among them states this fixed collider formula.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The universal source-preserving extension is proved for arbitrary normalized tables, including degenerate treatment marginals and zero-mass natural-treatment strata.  Its product-root assumption remains load-bearing: allowing a root shared by \(X\) and \(Z\), or otherwise correlating \(U0\) and \(V0\), can move the target outside the independent-source interval.  The at-most-eight-point private-root bound is a constructive upper bound, not an optimal-support theorem.
body.honest_scope: The proved result concerns only the fixed binary graph \(X\to Y\leftarrow Z\) with the two stated independent shared roots, private outcome noise, the two complete intervention tables, and the risk under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0)\).  Structural zeros are included.  A strictly positive-width conclusion is valid only under the additional interior condition \(0<p,r<1\); support faces may point-identify the risk.  Correlated or dependence-budget shared roots, different study populations, a simultaneous region for all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, minimal support, tie-optimal inference, a general thicket compiler, and any field-tier claim remain outside scope.  If regime \(B\) is omitted, the mass accounting gives \(q\in[a,a+1-p]\); symmetrically, omitting regime \(A\) gives \(q\in[b,b+1-r]\).
